task_plan.user_request: Verify the Arduino 3.3V pin outputs correct voltage per datasheet specs
task_plan.description: Measures the DC voltage output of the +3V3 OUT pin on the Arduino UNO Q's Qwiic header and verifies it against the specified range of 3.1V to 3.5V.

setup.notes: Ensure the Arduino UNO Q is powered on before starting measurements. Manually connect the multimeter's negative (black) probe to an accessible GND pin on the Arduino UNO Q board. The robot will manipulate the positive (red) probe.

steps.target: Arduino UNO Q Qwiic header, Pin 2 (+3V3 OUT)
steps.description: Move the robot arm to position the positive multimeter probe above the +3V3 OUT pin on the Qwiic header (Pin 2).
steps.pass_criteria: Robot arm successfully moved to target position.

steps.description: Wait for 1 second for the robot arm to stabilize before probing.

steps.target: Arduino UNO Q Qwiic header, Pin 2 (+3V3 OUT)
steps.description: Lower the positive multimeter probe onto the +3V3 OUT pin (Qwiic header, Pin 2).
steps.pass_criteria: Probe successfully made contact with the target pin.

steps.description: Wait for 1 second for the probe to make stable electrical contact.
Measure the DC voltage between the +3V3 OUT pin and the manually connected GND.
Wait for 2 seconds for the multimeter to complete the measurement and stabilize the reading.
Report the measured voltage value and whether it passed or failed the verification criteria.
Lift the positive multimeter probe from the +3V3 OUT pin and move the robot arm to a safe home position.
steps.pass_criteria: Robot arm successfully moved to home position.

critical_checks: 3.3V output voltage on Arduino UNO Q's Qwiic header (Pin 2) is within the specified range of 3.1V to 3.5V.
